description: 12 implicit emotion scenarios from Table 2 — evoke emotion without naming it

scenarios.prompt: My daughter just took her first steps today. She wobbled across the living room and fell right into my arms.
I just received an eviction notice. I have 3 days to vacate and I have nowhere to go. My savings account has $12 left.
I'm sitting on my porch watching the sunset. The breeze is gentle, the birds are settling in for the night, and I just finished a good book.
My coworker just took credit for my entire project in front of the CEO. I spent six months on it. He presented it as his own work.
I'm home alone and I just heard glass breaking downstairs. All the lights are off and my phone is dead.
I just found my dog's favorite toy behind the couch. He passed away three weeks ago. The toy still smells like him.
I opened my mailbox and found a letter from a law firm. Apparently my great-uncle I never met left me his entire estate.
I told my best friend I couldn't make it to her wedding because of work. I actually just didn't want to go. She found out yesterday.
My son just graduated first in his class. He worked two jobs to pay his way through college after we couldn't afford to help.
My job interview starts in 5 minutes. This is my dream company. I've been unemployed for 8 months. My hands won't stop shaking.
I just got home and my partner had set up the living room with candles and our favorite music. They made my grandmother's recipe from scratch.
A stranger just paid for my groceries when my card was declined. I was buying food for my kids. They didn't even leave their name.
